review_candidates.title: Woreda Program Officer

The organization partners with communities and government structures to expand access to quality education and strengthen protective systems for children. Each year, Imagine1day supports learning opportunities for more than 500,000 children, including 186,570 primary-age out-of-school children. Its programs span ten regions and 1,105 schools, improving teaching quality, community engagement, and local leadership capacity. Team members join a mission-driven environment dedicated to long-term, sustainable change for children and families. Vacancy Position Project External or Internal Woreda Program Officer Every Girl in School, Every Girl with a Choice Reports to Program Coordinator/RPM, with technical guidance from the CIFF Program Manager and ECM Specialist Duty station / coverage One officer based in each target woreda; responsible for 10 schools and surrounding communities Contract period 12 months with possibility of extension Program geography Salary Gubalafto, Kacha Bira, Boloso Sore, or Ginir (one position per woreda) As per the organization salary scale 1. Job Purpose Coordinate and assure high-quality day-to-day implementation of the CIFF program in one target woreda, covering 10 schools and their surrounding communities. The Woreda Program Officer is the primary field coordination point for schools, woreda offices and community structures and is responsible for implementation planning, girls’ identification and follow-up, activity quality, stakeholder coordination, monitoring, risk identification, documentation, timely reporting and corrective action. 2. Key ResponsibilitiesA. Woreda and school implementation ·      Prepare detailed woreda-level implementation schedules and coordinate delivery across the assigned 10 schools and communities. ·      Coordinate school/community mapping, verification and enrolment of vulnerable adolescent girls and support confidential tailored education/protection plans and monthly follow-up. ·      Support delivery of learning/MHH assistance, remedial and catch-up support, disability referrals/accommodation, flexible pathways and AEP linkages as applicable. ·      Support school focal persons to operate attendance, dropout, disengagement, child-marriage and protection-risk early-warning and follow-up processes. B. Safe, inclusive and gender-responsive schools ·      Coordinate participatory school safety, accessibility, MHH, safeguarding and gender-responsiveness assessments. ·      Support schools to prepare, implement and review protection, inclusion, safety and retention action plans integrated with school-improvement processes. ·      Coordinate teacher/school-leader training, school-based coaching, termly safety walks and action-plan reviews. ·      Support confidential, accessible complaints/reporting mechanisms, referral information and functioning girls’ clubs/mentorship arrangements. C. Community child-marriage prevention ·      Coordinate formative inquiry, community mobilization and structured intergenerational dialogues in the assigned woreda. ·      Support community child-marriage prevention platforms and faith/traditional leaders, boys, men and youth champions to implement agreed actions. ·      Work with the ECM Specialist to ensure dialogue quality, rights-based messaging, inclusion and monitoring of social resistance/backlash. ·      Maintain constructive engagement with parents/caregivers and community structures to strengthen attendance, retention and delayed marriage. D. Government coordination and referrals ·      Maintain routine coordination with woreda administration, education, Women and Social Affairs, health, justice, police, civil registration and other relevant actors. ·      Support mapping, testing and review of survivor-centred referral pathways and follow up agreed service/coordination gaps. ·      Facilitate multisectoral coordination meetings, joint performance reviews, supervision and use of relevant SOPs/job aids. ·      Support integration of project indicators and girl-level risk tracking into woreda review/EMIS routines where feasible. E. Monitoring, safeguarding and reporting ·      Maintain complete, accurate and timely implementation records, participant/service data, activity evidence and follow-up actions in coordination with the Impact/MEAL team. ·      Monitor progress against woreda targets, activity quality, inclusion, safeguarding, referrals, risks and community feedback and initiate corrective action. ·      Immediately escalate safeguarding concerns, serious protection risks, security/access issues and other high-risk events through approved channels. ·      Submit timely weekly/monthly/quarterly updates as required and contribute to learning reviews, data-quality checks, assessments and donor reporting. F. Operational coordination ·      Coordinate field logistics, procurement requests, activity advances/liquidation, materials distribution and asset use in line with organizational procedures. ·      Support AEP facilitators and other field personnel with implementation coordination while maintaining clear accountability and documentation. ·      Promote economical use of resources and verify that program inputs reach intended girls, schools and community structures. 3. Key Performance Areas / Expected Results ·      Each officer provides consistent implementation coverage to 10 schools and surrounding communities. ·      Vulnerable girls in the assigned woreda are identified, verified, supported and followed up through secure, timely processes. ·      Assigned schools use functional early-warning/follow-up arrangements and implement school protection, inclusion, safety and retention actions. ·      Community dialogues, prevention platforms and champions in the assigned woreda are implemented to agreed quality standards and documented. ·      Woreda referral pathways and multisectoral coordination mechanisms are functional and periodically reviewed. ·      Program data, safeguarding/risk escalation, activity documentation and reports are timely, complete and accurate. 4. Minimum Qualifications and Experience ·      Bachelor’s degree (master’s degree preferred) in education, social work, sociology, gender studies, development studies, community development or a related field. ·      Typically, 4+ years of relevant field experience from international and national NGOs in education, adolescent-girls programming, child protection, gender, community mobilization or development programming. ·      Experience coordinating with woreda government offices, schools and community structures and managing multiple field activities simultaneously. ·      Practical understanding of safeguarding, confidentiality, referrals, inclusive programming and results-based monitoring. ·      Strong facilitation, organization, documentation and problem-solving skills; proficiency in the relevant local language is strongly preferred, with working English for reporting. ·      Ability and willingness to travel frequently among assigned schools and communities, including remote locations, subject to safety procedures. 5. Core Competencies ·      Field implementation and coordination ·      Community facilitation and stakeholder engagement ·      Girl-centred and safeguarding-sensitive practice ·      Monitoring, documentation and timely reporting ·      Problem solving and corrective action ·      Teamwork and respectful communication ·      Integrity, confidentiality and accountability 6. Key Working Relationships ·      Internal: Program Coordinators, RPM, CIFF Program Manager; ECM Specialist; AEP facilitators; Impact/MEAL; regional Program/GESI/Safeguarding/Operations/Finance teams. ·      External: Woreda administration and sector offices; school leaders/teachers; PTSAs/school boards; girls’ clubs; community care/protection structures; faith/traditional leaders; families and service providers. 7. Safeguarding and Professional Conduct The postholder must comply with Imagine1day safeguarding, PSEAH/PASH, child-protection, data-protection, confidentiality, code-of-conduct and do-no-harm requirements. Safety, dignity, informed choice, confidentiality and the best interests of girls take precedence over program targets. Any safeguarding concern must be handled through approved reporting and survivor-centred referral procedures.

Grey Shell Development works in parallel to NGEN’s core product and supply chain organization. NGEN is a preferred vendor, but we remain manufacturer-agnostic for customers sourcing other brands. Our team works hard and maintains a collaborative, respectful, and supportive culture. We value colleagues with a sense of humor who see themselves as “builders” and want to make a real impact. THE OPPORTUNITY: Our Grey Shell Development team is growing and we’re adding a senior technical leader to make sure every system on a site works together as one: power, cooling, controls, and every interface in between. As VP Data Center Systems Integration, you’ll take full command of technical system integration across Grey Shell Development’s data center work, reporting directly to our Chief Development Officer. This role sits between early-stage concept design and detailed project execution. Our design team leads conceptual work and test fits, while our delivery and procurement teams need firm quantities, requirements, and dates. You’ll own the technical layer that connects them, engineering how power, thermal, and controls systems come together on a site and translating design intent into the detail that execution runs on. Grey Shell Development is manufacturer-agnostic: our customers source equipment from leading domestic and international brands, and your focus is making the right combination work as one integrated system. You’ll also be a visible technical presence with our customers. Alongside our Chief Development Officer, who leads executive-level relationships, you’ll help keep customer conversations focused on the outcomes and milestones that matter most, then carry the technical depth forward with customers’ engineering teams. You’ll lead a team of engineers who execute integrated system scopes, and you’ll shape the integration standards, reference designs, and design review processes that are still being built. This role is designed to strengthen the leadership team around it, giving our design, delivery, and executive leaders a true technical partner on every project. If you’re drawn to systems-level problems, energized by connecting big-picture design with on-the-ground execution, and ready to build an integration function from the ground up, this is the role for you. WHAT IT IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT: This role is focused entirely on system-level integration and deployment for data center projects. Product development is not part of this role in any form. You won’t design, develop, or engineer equipment or products, including any manufactured or offered by NGEN, and you won’t take part in product development or product roadmap decisions. Your work is integrating selected equipment, from any manufacturer, into complete, working systems for our customers. YOUR MISSION: Own technical system integration across Grey Shell Development’s data center projects, defining how power, thermal, and controls systems work together as a complete, deployable solution Lead a team of engineers responsible for executing integrated system scopes, setting priorities, standards, and clear ownership for how the work gets done Translate conceptual designs and test fits into actionable requirements for procurement and project delivery, including quantities, interfaces, and schedule milestones Serve as the primary technical counterpart for project delivery and procurement, giving clear answers on what is needed, how much, and when Bridge the design and delivery teams, aligning priorities and sequencing so conceptual work and execution stay in step Shape overall system deployment strategy for data center programs, working alongside the teams that own equipment selection and specification Develop integrated system architectures, including single-line diagrams, interface control documents, and integration specifications spanning power distribution, generation, energy storage, and cooling Define the electrical, mechanical, controls, and communications interfaces between major equipment, site systems, and building infrastructure, regardless of manufacturer Support manufacturer-agnostic solutions, integrating equipment from leading domestic and international brands in line with each customer’s sourcing preferences Support our Chief Development Officer in customer meetings, keeping discussions at the right altitude and following up directly with customer engineering teams on technical detail Run technical design reviews with customers, EPCs, consulting engineers, and utilities, resolving integration issues long before they reach the field Build Grey Shell Development’s integration playbook: reference designs, interface standards, design review gates, and lessons-learned processes that scale across projects Provide technical scope definition and integration risk input for commercial proposals and bids Shape integrated testing and commissioning strategy alongside our project execution teams Ensure integrated solutions meet applicable codes, standards, and reliability requirements YOU’LL WIN US OVER WITH THIS KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE: You have 10+ years of experience in data center, mission critical, or critical power infrastructure, including at least 5 years leading technical teams You have a bachelor’s degree in electrical or mechanical engineering, or equivalent professional experience; a PE license is a strong asset You’ve led system integration on hyperscale, colocation, or large enterprise data center projects, ideally across powered shell, Grey shell, or prefabricated and modular delivery models You bring deep system-level knowledge of critical power architecture, including switchgear, UPS, generation, energy storage, and power distribution, along with a solid working understanding of thermal systems You’ve worked directly with customer engineering teams, consulting engineers, and EPCs, and you’re credible presenting technical solutions to senior stakeholders You have strong command of the codes and standards that govern data center power and cooling, such as NEC, NFPA 70E, UL, IEEE, and Uptime Institute tier classifications Experience with liquid cooling or high-density AI workloads is a meaningful plus Experience with utility interconnection or on-site and behind-the-meter generation is a plus Experience building an integration or applications engineering function at a growing company would put a smile on our face WHO YOU ARE: You’re a builder. The gaps between systems are your favorite part of the job, and you’d rather design the process that closes them once than work around them project after project. You’re a systems thinker. You see how every component, interface, and dependency on a site fits together, and you can explain it clearly to someone who only sees one piece. You’re a natural partner. You get real energy from making the leaders around you more effective, and you help teams with different working styles find a shared rhythm. You know how to read the room with customers. You keep conversations focused on what matters at each stage, save the deep detail for the right audience, and stay steady when the questions get hard. You’re comfortable with ambiguity and energized by building. Grey Shell Development is growing fast and many of the systems and processes around this function are still being shaped. You see that as an opportunity. They are our greatest resource, and without them, sustainable change is not possible.  These leaders are community development experts, pastors, team builders, and co-laborers for Christ on the journey to end poverty. They collaboratively mobilize the local church, government agencies, and other entities to engage the community's needs with crucial initiatives that produce community resilience, health, and progress. Inclusive - We are a wide table:  we believe anyone who wants a seat at the table of doing good deserves to be here. That means we have a wide range of personalities and perspectives surrounding us, and we think that’s beautiful. We recognize tension, but prioritize connection and empathy. Collaborative - We believe our greatest gift is one another. Collaboration is how our best work gets done - collaborating with our friends, donors, international partners, and each other is what makes us great. Innovative - We are smart, fun, and entrepreneurial. Being part of our team means taking initiative and problem-solving some of the most unique issues, from small to large. Empowering - We exist to empower people around the world, and we take that value to heart. This includes empowering our team, donors, and friends. We believe everyone’s voice matters and seek to see all people live out their fullest potential.  Committed - Development work is hard; it’s not a quick fix and takes time. We are committed to the partners, families, and children we serve around the world. We’re in this for the long haul, and we believe true partnership only exists with true commitment. That commitment is a two-way street in all of our relationships. We strive to uphold that commitment in all ways - to our donors to utilize the resources they give for the greatest impact, to international partners to stand by them and work together for good, to the people we serve to develop in healthy, sustainable, dignified ways, and to each other to see this work through.  Friendship   - We value the collaborative relationships we develop here at Help One Now. We think the best way to stay committed and connected is to remember that we are building friendships. We create a team atmosphere; we love to have fun together, work hard, and play hard. We take that value into every facet of our organization - our global partnerships, team building, donor journey, and board relationships. This position reports directly to the President and Chief of Staff, working in partnership with the Advancement and Marketing team to build a healthy new-donor pipeline, expand Help One Now's network, and cultivate relationships for long-term stewardship and growth. The ideal candidate lives in or near the following locations: Austin, TX; Birmingham, AL; Nashville, TN; or Atlanta, GA, or is willing to relocate. Support and mentor social service providers, justice system actors and partner organizations to ensure survivors of human trafficking receive safe, trauma-informed, and survivor-centered services. Provide technical guidance on case management, survivor protection, restoration planning and community reintegration. Support survivors through key stages of the justice process, including court preparation and coordination of services where needed. Collaborate with partner agencies to assess and address safety, protection and support needs for survivors. Partnership Building & Stakeholder Engagement Build and maintain strong relationships with government institutions, NGOs, shelters, social welfare agencies and other service providers. Strengthen collaboration between social service providers and justice system stakeholders to improve outcomes for survivors. Facilitate multidisciplinary meetings and promote effective coordination among stakeholders involved in survivor care. Develop and maintain a network of organizations capable of providing high-quality support services for survivors. Contribute to advocacy and awareness-raising initiatives that strengthen the response to human trafficking. Training, Capacity Building & Program Development Design and deliver professional training on trauma-informed care, crisis intervention, survivor-centered practices and case management. Mentor and coach partner organizations to strengthen their capacity to support survivors effectively. Assess strengths and gaps within existing social service systems and recommend improvements. Contribute expertise, tools and recommendations that enhance IJM's survivor support strategies and program quality. Monitoring, Reporting & Compliance Maintain accurate records and documentation in compliance with GDPR and organizational requirements. Analyze case trends, service delivery gaps and stakeholder needs to inform program development. Contribute to monitoring, evaluation and reporting activities, including grant reporting where applicable. Prepare high-quality reports, documentation and recommendations related to survivor services and program outcomes. Minimum 5 years of experience working directly with survivors of trauma, violence, exploitation, trafficking, or other vulnerable populations. Experience delivering training, mentoring, coaching or capacity-building initiatives. Experience building partnerships and working collaboratively with NGOs, government agencies, shelters or social service providers. Experience working within multidisciplinary environments involving social services, protection services or the justice sector. Clinical or therapeutic experience is an advantage. Experience in anti-human trafficking, child protection, gender-based violence or related fields is a strong advantage. Strong expertise in trauma-informed care and survivor-centered approaches. Ability to develop and deliver training programs in Polish and English. Strong stakeholder engagement, relationship-building and facilitation skills. Excellent case analysis, documentation and report-writing abilities. Ability to assess service systems, identify gaps and propose practical improvements. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and digital case management or reporting systems. Fluent written and spoken Polish and English. Commitment to IJM's mission, values and professionalism. Strong interpersonal and influencing skills. Ability to build trust and credibility with diverse stakeholders. Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail. High level of integrity, discretion and professionalism. Resilient, adaptable and able to perform effectively in challenging situations. Proactive, solutions-oriented and able to work independently. Collaborative team player with strong communication skills. Ability to travel within Poland and Europe, up to 30% of the time. Polish driver’s license is a plus.
